**Exercise 2(a): Simulating a VAR(1) in R**

```{r}
#rm(list = ls())
library(dplyr)
```

We need to simulate 500 observations using mvrnorm().

Step 1: Define the parameters

```{r}

n <- 500

A <- matrix(c(0.5, 0.1,
              0.2, 0.4), nrow = 2)

Sigma <- matrix(c(1, 0.3,                # covariance matrix
                  0.3, 1), nrow = 2)

```

Step 2: Generate the errors

```{r}

library(MASS)

set.seed(23)

epsilon <- mvrnorm(n,c(0,0),Sigma) # from MASS package

dim(epsilon)
class(epsilon)
  
```

Step 3: Simulate the VAR(1)

```{r}


Y <- matrix(0, nrow = n, ncol = 2)

for (t in 2:n) {
  Y[t, ] <- A %*% Y[t-1, ] + epsilon[t, ]
}

colnames(Y) <- c("Y1", "Y2")

matplot(Y, type = "l", lty = 1,
        xlab = "Time", ylab = "Value")
legend("topright", legend = colnames(Y),
       col = 1:2, lty = 1)
dim(Y)
head(Y)

```
**Implementing the estimators**

Estimated coefficients matrix (A hat):

```{r}


# Current and lagged observations
Y_current <- Y[2:n, ]
Y_lag <- Y[1:(n-1), ]

# Estimate A
A_hat <- t(Y_current) %*% Y_lag %*%
         solve(t(Y_lag) %*% Y_lag)

A_hat


```

Estimated residuals:

```{r}


# Calculate residuals
residuals <- Y_current - Y_lag %*% t(A_hat)

# Check dimensions
dim(residuals)

# Display first residuals
head(residuals)


```
Estimated covariance matrix:

```{r}

Sigma_hat <- t(residuals) %*% residuals / (n - 1)

Sigma_hat

```

**Monte Carlo simulation**

Initialize storage matrices:

```{r}

nsim <- 1000
n <- 500

# Store 4 coefficients of A
A_estimates <- matrix(NA, nrow = nsim, ncol = 4)

# Store 4 elements of Sigma
Sigma_estimates <- matrix(NA, nrow = nsim, ncol = 4)

colnames(A_estimates) <- c("a11", "a21", "a12", "a22")
colnames(Sigma_estimates) <- c("s11", "s21", "s12", "s22")

```

Step 1: Build the Monte Carlo loop

```{r}

set.seed(23)

for (i in 1:nsim) {

  # 1. Generate new errors
  epsilon <- mvrnorm(
    n = n,
    mu = c(0, 0),
    Sigma = Sigma
  )

  # 2. Simulate a new VAR(1)
  Y <- matrix(0, nrow = n, ncol = 2)

  for (t in 2:n) {
    Y[t, ] <- A %*% Y[t-1, ] + epsilon[t, ]
  }

  # 3. Construct current and lagged observations
  Y_current <- Y[2:n, ]
  Y_lag <- Y[1:(n-1), ]

  # 4. Estimate A
  A_hat <- t(Y_current) %*% Y_lag %*%
           solve(t(Y_lag) %*% Y_lag)

  # 5. Compute residuals
  residuals <- Y_current - Y_lag %*% t(A_hat)

  # 6. Estimate Sigma
  Sigma_hat <- t(residuals) %*% residuals / (n - 1)

  # 7. Store estimates
  A_estimates[i, ] <- as.vector(A_hat)
  Sigma_estimates[i, ] <- as.vector(Sigma_hat)
}

```

Step 2: Examine the estimates

```{r}

round(colMeans(A_estimates),4)
round(colMeans(Sigma_estimates),4)

# These calculate the average estimated value of each parameter across the 1,000 simulations.
```
Step 3: Plot the boxplots

```{r}


par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

# Boxplots for A
boxplot(A_estimates,
        main = "Estimates of A",
        ylab = "Estimated coefficients",
        col = "lightblue")

points(1:4, as.vector(A),
       col = "red", pch = 19)

# Boxplots for Sigma
boxplot(Sigma_estimates,
        main = "Estimates of Sigma",
        ylab = "Estimated covariances",
        col = "lightgreen")

points(1:4, as.vector(Sigma),
       col = "red", pch = 19)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

```

**Exercise 3: Dynamic Factor Models (DFM)**

Load and visualize the UK exports data

```{r}
library(sparseDFM)


# Explore the dataset
str(exports)
dim(exports)

colnames(exports)[1:9]
#head(exports,1)

```
Extract the 9 target series

```{r}

# Extract the 9 target series
targets <- exports[, 1:9]

# Remove incomplete rows
targets_clean <- targets[complete.cases(targets), ] # complete.cases() returns TRUE for rows containing no missing values in the selected columns (we keep only those rows)

# Check dimensions
dim(targets_clean)

```

Plot the target series

```{r}

# Shorten series names for the legend
target_names <- sub("^target\\.", "", colnames(targets_clean))

# Plot the 9 target series
ts.plot(targets_clean,
        col = 1:9,
        lty = 1,
        main = "UK Exports: 9 Target Series",
        xlab = "Time",
        ylab = "Exports")

legend("topleft",
       legend = target_names,
       col = 1:9,
       lty = 1,
       cex = 0.6,
       bty = "n")

```

```{r}

args(transformData)
?transformData

```

**b) Apply transformData()**

```{r}

# Apply first differences to all 9 series
stationary_transform <- rep(2, 9)

targets_diff <- transformData(
  X = as.matrix(targets_clean),
  stationary_transform = stationary_transform
)

dim(targets_diff)
```

Plot the transformed series

```{r}


# Remove rows with missing values after differencing
targets_diff <- targets_diff[
  complete.cases(targets_diff), ,
  drop = FALSE
]

# Plot transformed series
ts.plot(targets_diff,
        col = 1:9,
        lty = 1,
        main = "UK Exports: First Differences",
        xlab = "Year",
        ylab = "Change in exports")

legend("topleft",
       legend = sub("^target\\.", "",
                    colnames(targets)),
       col = 1:9,
       lty = 1,
       cex = 0.6,
       bty = "n")


```

```{r}

# Apply first differences to the complete dataset
# (9 targets + 436 indicators)

X_clean <- exports[complete.cases(exports), , drop = FALSE]

stationary_transform_full <- rep(2, ncol(X_clean))

X_diff <- transformData(
  X = as.matrix(X_clean),
  stationary_transform = stationary_transform_full
)

# Remove incomplete observations after differencing
X_diff <- X_diff[
  complete.cases(X_diff), ,
  drop = FALSE
]

dim(X_diff)
sum(is.na(X_diff))

```

**c) Determine the optimal number of factors**

```{r}
args(tuneFactors)
?tuneFactors

```

Select the number of factors

```{r}

# Select the optimal number of factors using Bai-Ng IC2
r_opt <- tuneFactors(
  X = X_diff,
  type = 2,
  standardize = TRUE,
  r.max = 15,
  plot = TRUE
)

r_opt

```

**d) Fit the Dynamic Factor Model using sparseDFM()**

```{r}
?sparseDFM
```

Fit the standard DFM:

```{r}
library(sparseDFM)

# Standard Dynamic Factor Model (alg = 'EM')
fit_dfm <- sparseDFM(
  X = X_diff,
  r = 7,
  alg = "EM",
  standardize = TRUE
)


```

Fit the sparse DFM:

```{r}

# Sparse Dynamic Factor Model
# Keep the 9 export targets unpenalized
fit_sdfm <- sparseDFM(
  X = X_diff,
  r = 7,
  q = 9,
  alg = "EM-sparse",
  standardize = TRUE
)

```

Check the fitted models :

```{r}
# Dimensions of the estimated factor and loading matrices
dim(fit_dfm$state$factors)
dim(fit_dfm$params$Lambda)

dim(fit_sdfm$state$factors)
dim(fit_sdfm$params$Lambda)

# Check convergence
fit_dfm$em$converged
fit_sdfm$em$converged
```
**e) Plot the estimated factors and loadings**

```{r}

# Estimated factors: standard DFM
plot(fit_dfm, type = "factor")

# Estimated factors: sparse DFM
plot(fit_sdfm, type = "factor")

```

**Factor loadings**

Heatmap - Standard DFM model:

```{r}
# Extract loading matrices
L_dfm <- fit_dfm$params$Lambda
L_sdfm <- fit_sdfm$params$Lambda

# Plot standard DFM loadings
image(
  x = 1:nrow(L_dfm),
  y = 1:ncol(L_dfm),
  z = L_dfm,
  col = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(100),
  xlab = "Series",
  ylab = "Factor",
  main = "Standard DFM: Factor Loadings",
  axes = FALSE
)

axis(2, at = 1:7, labels = paste0("F", 1:7))
axis(1, at = seq(1, nrow(L_dfm), by = 50))
```

Heatmap - Sparse DFM model:

```{r}
# Use the same color scale for both models
limit <- max(abs(c(L_dfm, L_sdfm)))

colors <- colorRampPalette(
  c("blue", "white", "red")
)(100)

image(
  x = 1:nrow(L_sdfm),
  y = 1:ncol(L_sdfm),
  z = L_sdfm,
  col = colors,
  zlim = c(-limit, limit),
  xlab = "Series",
  ylab = "Factor",
  main = "Sparse DFM: Factor Loadings",
  axes = FALSE
)

axis(2, at = 1:7, labels = paste0("F", 1:7))
axis(1, at = seq(1, nrow(L_sdfm), by = 50))
```

**Identify the indicator groups**

```{r}
# Extract the second part of each variable name
groups <- sub("^indicators\\.([^.]+)\\..*$", "\\1",
              colnames(X_diff))

# Keep export targets in their own group
groups[grepl("^target\\.", colnames(X_diff))] <- "target"

# Count variables in each group
table(groups)
```

Correct the group labels

```{r}

# Correct and standardize group labels
groups[groups == "target"] <- "TiG"
groups[groups == "iop"] <- "IoP"
groups[groups == "cpi"] <- "CPI"
groups[groups == "ppi"] <- "PPI"
groups[groups == "exchange"] <- "Exch"
groups[groups == "google"] <- "GT"
groups[groups %in% c("indicators.bci", "indicators.cci")] <- "Conf"

table(groups)
```

Identify which groups drive each factor

```{r}
# Average absolute sparse loading by indicator group
group_loading <- sapply(
  unique(groups),
  function(g) {
    colMeans(abs(L_sdfm[groups == g, , drop = FALSE]))
  }
)

rownames(group_loading) <- paste0("Factor ", 1:7)

round(group_loading, 3)
```

**f) Monte-Carlo simulation**

Check the fitted model parameters

```{r}
names(fit_sdfm$params)

str(fit_sdfm$params, max.level = 1)

names(fit_sdfm$state)
```
Run the Monte Carlo simulation

```{r}

library(MASS)

set.seed(23)

nsim <- 200
h <- 10

# Estimated sparse DFM parameters
A <- fit_sdfm$params$A
Lambda <- fit_sdfm$params$Lambda
Sigma_u <- fit_sdfm$params$Sigma_u
Sigma_epsilon <- fit_sdfm$params$Sigma_epsilon

# Last estimated factor values
F_last <- as.numeric(
  tail(fit_sdfm$state$factors, 1)
)

# Target series: first 9 variables
target_idx <- 1:9
target_names <- colnames(X_diff)[target_idx]

# Store simulated forecasts: month x target x simulation
sim_forecasts <- array(
  NA_real_,
  dim = c(h, 9, nsim)
)

# Monte Carlo simulation
for (s in 1:nsim) {

  F_current <- F_last

  for (t in 1:h) {

    # Simulate factor innovations
    u_t <- as.numeric(
      mvrnorm(1, mu = rep(0, 7), Sigma = Sigma_u)
    )

    # Forecast next factors
    F_current <- as.numeric(A %*% F_current + u_t)

    # Simulate observation errors for 9 targets
    epsilon_t <- rnorm(
      9,
      mean = 0,
      sd = sqrt(Sigma_epsilon[target_idx])
    )

    # Simulated target values (standardized differences)
    sim_forecasts[t, , s] <-
      as.numeric(Lambda[target_idx, ] %*% F_current) +
      epsilon_t
  }
}

# Compute 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles
forecast_quantiles <- apply(
  sim_forecasts,
  c(1, 2),
  quantile,
  probs = c(0.05, 0.50, 0.95)
)

dim(forecast_quantiles)
```

Plot the forecasts

```{r}

# Reverse standardization of the simulated differences
target_mean <- colMeans(X_diff)[1:9]
target_sd <- apply(X_diff[, 1:9], 2, sd)

sim_diff <- sweep(
  sim_forecasts, 2, target_sd, "*"
)

sim_diff <- sweep(
  sim_diff, 2, target_mean, "+"
)

# Convert monthly differences into export levels
last_levels <- as.numeric(
  tail(X_clean[, 1:9], 1)
)

sim_levels <- sim_diff

for (s in 1:nsim) {
  for (j in 1:9) {
    sim_levels[, j, s] <-
      last_levels[j] + cumsum(sim_diff[, j, s])
  }
}

# Prediction intervals and median forecasts
forecast_levels <- apply(
  sim_levels,
  c(1, 2),
  quantile,
  probs = c(0.05, 0.50, 0.95)
)

# Plot all nine targets
par(mfrow = c(3, 3), mar = c(3, 3, 3, 1))

for (j in 1:9) {

  lower <- forecast_levels[1, , j]
  median <- forecast_levels[2, , j]
  upper <- forecast_levels[3, , j]

  plot(
    1:h, median,
    type = "l",
    lwd = 2,
    col = "blue",
    ylim = range(lower, upper, last_levels[j]),
    xlab = "Months ahead",
    ylab = "Export level",
    main = sub("^target\\.", "", target_names[j])
  )

  polygon(
    c(1:h, h:1),
    c(lower, rev(upper)),
    col = adjustcolor("lightblue", alpha.f = 0.5),
    border = NA
  )

  lines(1:h, median, col = "blue", lwd = 2)
  lines(1:h, lower, col = "red", lty = 2)
  lines(1:h, upper, col = "red", lty = 2)

  abline(h = last_levels[j], col = "gray50", lty = 3)
}

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```
**g) Identify COVID-19 and the 2009 recession**

```{r}
# Estimated factors
F_est <- fit_sdfm$state$factors

# Reconstruct monthly dates from the original dataset
all_dates <- time(exports)

# Keep dates corresponding to complete observations
clean_dates <- all_dates[complete.cases(exports)]

# First differencing removes the first observation
diff_dates <- tail(clean_dates, nrow(X_diff))

# Check alignment
stopifnot(length(diff_dates) == nrow(F_est))

# Economic event periods
recession <- diff_dates >= 2008.5 & diff_dates < 2010
covid <- diff_dates >= 2020 & diff_dates < 2021

# Verify that observations were selected
cat("Recession observations:", sum(recession), "\n")
cat("COVID observations:", sum(covid), "\n")

# Compare factor movements relative to their usual variability
F_scaled <- scale(F_est)

recession_strength <- apply(
  abs(F_scaled[recession, , drop = FALSE]), 2, max
)

covid_strength <- apply(
  abs(F_scaled[covid, , drop = FALSE]), 2, max
)

names(recession_strength) <- paste0("Factor ", 1:7)
names(covid_strength) <- paste0("Factor ", 1:7)

cat("\n2008–2009 recession:\n")
print(sort(recession_strength, decreasing = TRUE))

cat("\nCOVID-19 period:\n")
print(sort(covid_strength, decreasing = TRUE))
```
